label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT - Monday at Embakasi: casuals' pay brief for Brian

Brian,

You asked for something you can read on Sunday so you're not guessing on Monday morning. This is it. It's built from the emails, DMs and docs as of Saturday night. Where I don't know something, I say so.

1. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED

Friday's casual pay was meant to go out by bank transfer. The bank rejected the whole file at validation on Friday afternoon. After their platform upgrade on 25 November, files have to use a new template, and ours didn't match (one column was too long). Nothing in the file was processed, so nobody was paid, not even partly. We only saw the rejection after the bank's cut-off, so there was nothing more to be done that day.

On Saturday morning Njeri approved paying everyone through M-Pesa instead. Peninah has been checking the phone numbers against the list. 198 of the 212 are confirmed. 14 she couldn't reach, mostly the newer loaders from the Athi River intake.

That's the whole story, and it's a short one. It was a payment error on our side. The guys did nothing wrong, and nobody's pay is in doubt. It's late, and that's all. When you say "our mistake", say it as the company. Don't blame the bank and don't name a person or a department.

2. WHEN THE MONEY LANDS

The realistic time from finance is Monday by 11am. Kevin was clear he won't promise anything earlier, so neither should you. This is a realistic time and not a guarantee, which is why step 4 below matters.

The 14 unreachable numbers are separate. Their money can only go once Peninah has the right numbers, and I don't yet have a time for them. Don't give them one. Rent is due on the 1st, which is Tuesday, so if the batch lands Monday it still lands in time. Some of the guys will be counting on that.

3. WHAT YOU CAN PROMISE AND WHAT YOU MUSTN'T

You can promise these. Njeri has approved all of them.
- Everyone on the affected list is being paid in full by M-Pesa, with 11am Monday as the realistic time.
- Every casual on the list gets KES 500 extra for Monday's lunch and fare, paid in the same M-Pesa batch.
- The M-Pesa charges are on the company. Nothing is deducted from anyone.
- An apology from management, in person. Njeri asked for this and wants you to do it, since I'm travelling.
- You'll be at the depot until the money lands, and if the time is going to slip you'll tell them yourself. Say it at 10:30, not at 11:30.
- Peninah is on site from 7:30 with the list and her laptop. She can print payslips for anyone who wants one, and the 14 can give her correct numbers face to face.

Don't promise or say these:
- Any time we can't keep. Remember Mombasa in 2024. The supervisor said "by lunch", the money came at 4pm, and half the shift sat down. Never again a time we can't keep.
- Words like "tomorrow", "soon" or "by lunch". The guys were told "tomorrow" three days running last time, so they won't hear those words kindly. Give a clock time, and say what you'll do if it moves.
- Anything earlier than 11am.
- Any time for the 14 yet.
- Extra money or compensation beyond the KES 500.
- Anything about contracts, discipline, dismissal or names. Our procedure says no one is dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day, and I want that followed to the letter.
- Reasons you're not sure of. If someone asks why it couldn't go over the weekend, "I don't know, I'll find out" beats a guess that turns out wrong. (The honest short version is that the approval and the number checks came Saturday, and Monday morning is the earliest finance would commit to.)

4. SUNDAY, BEFORE YOU SLEEP

Three quick things.
- Call Kevin. Confirm 11am still holds. Ask how you'll know the moment the batch is released, ideally a message or screenshot you can show Ouma. Ask when the 14 will be paid once their numbers are fixed. If Kevin gives you any time other than 11am, use his, not mine.
- Message Joseph so he knows you're coming personally and you're at the depot at 5:30. He asked me who is coming, and he'll calm the guys better if he can tell them. Don't give him a money time to pass on until Kevin has confirmed it.
- Work out the latest time loading can start and still get the Kisumu trucks out by 9, and have the mill's number ready. You know that better than I do.

5. MONDAY MORNING

At 5:30 you're at the depot. Speak to Joseph first and find out where the mood really is.

Before you face the group, find Ouma and talk to him alone. He's loud, but he's not a bad man. He has four kids and rent, and the money is what he's worried about. Listen first. Don't open with the procedure. Tell him straight what happened, apologise, and give him the time and the extras. Ask him what the guys need to see in order to load. If you can honestly give it, give it. If you can't, say so.

Then address the whole group. Don't go in defensive. They were let down, and it was our mistake, not theirs. Keep it short:
- Apologise first, on behalf of management.
- Say plainly what happened.
- Tell them what is coming: full pay, the KES 500, no charges deducted, and 11am as the realistic time.
- Tell them you'll be at the depot until it lands, and that you'll update them at 10:30 whatever the news.
- Tell the 14 to see Peninah when she arrives at 7:30.
- Take questions and answer straight.

6. IF OUMA'S GROUP WON'T LOAD

First, this is not a disciplinary matter. Under our procedure, a stoppage is not a grievance channel, but it is handled by Operations and HR together, and no one is dismissed or threatened on the day. So no talk of contracts and no "load or else", however hot it gets.

If they won't load:
1. Don't argue in front of the group. Take Ouma aside again, ask what would make them load, and offer only what you can truly deliver.
2. Message me straight away so HR is in it. I'm on WhatsApp until I board and in the air after that. I'll pick it up as soon as I land. Don't hold up the other steps waiting for me. Peninah can speak to the payroll facts, but she isn't HR cover.
3. Protect the 9am slot without pushing anyone. You'll know the latest start time from Sunday. If loading hasn't started by then, call the mill and ask for a later offloading slot instead of leaning on the guys. If anyone chooses to load, that's their choice. No pressure on them, and no turning them against the others.
4. Keep short notes: times, who said what, what you offered. Send them to me.
5. Don't lecture anyone about the grievance route on the day. After Monday, grievances go to Joseph first and then to HR within 48 hours, and I'll deal with those.

A late truck we can recover from. A crew that feels threatened or humiliated is much harder to recover from.

7. REACHING ME

Please WhatsApp me before I board if anything changes. I'm up from 4:30. After that I'm in the air for a bit, and I'll be back on my phone once I land in Entebbe.

You've dealt with worse than this, and I'd rather it were you in front of them than anyone else. Thank you for taking it.

Achieng
